subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO & Concurrency qualification

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO & Concurrency qualification

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side on the performance/SLO items we discussed: 

- Recap: ACME is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing summarization and chat features that are latency-sensitive (p95 target) and have periodic high-concurrency bursts during product launches.
- Info we still need from you to finalize a rate/quotas recommendation:
  * Target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and typical response lengths (tokens).
  * Expected sustained RPS and peak burst RPS by endpoint (or by user cohort).
  * Concurrency definition you care about (parallel requests vs. open streaming connections).
  * Any long-lived streaming use cases and expected connection counts.

Attached: redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf (initial template we use for sizing) — feel free to ignore the numbers for now.

Next steps: if you can send the traffic numbers above, we’ll run a quick sizing and propose either: a Dedicated/Reserved capacity commit or a Hosted plan with custom quota increases. We can also schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Logan) and solutions engineer (Laura) to validate assumptions.

Proposed slots: Wed 10/14 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 10/15 11:00–12:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acmecorp.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO & Concurrency qualification

Marissa —

Appreciate the follow-up and the template. Some quick numbers from our infra/product team to help you size:

- Traffic profile (expected for Q1 pilot):
  * Avg sustained RPS across endpoints: ~800 RPS
  * Peak sustained RPS (promo days): ~2,500 RPS for ~2 hours
  * Typical response length: 512 tokens (avg), 1,024 tokens (max)
  * Concurrency: we consider "concurrent" = parallel active requests; peak concurrent active requests ~= 1,200 during bursts (mostly short requests ~200–400ms), plus ~300 long-lived streaming connections for live summaries.
- Latency SLOs: p50 ~ 80–120ms; p95 target <= 250ms for 512-token responses. p99 is a softer target but we'd like visibility.
- Burst pattern: predictable — marketing-triggered launches that last 1–3 hours, then fall back to baseline.

We can share a 24-hour sample of real traffic (anonymized) if that helps. Attached an infra summary (acme-infra-summary.pdf) with current autoscaling configs.

For quotas, we need clarity on: concurrent request limits per API key, per-tenant token-per-minute caps, and soft vs. hard rate limits (and recommended backoff behavior).

I can do Wed 10/14 10:00 PT for the deep-dive.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Product Manager, ACME Corp
ben.carter@acmecorp.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO & Concurrency qualification

Ben —

Great, thanks for the numbers — super helpful. Based on what you shared we have a couple of immediate recommendations and questions. High-level proposal below; we’ll confirm details during the deep-dive: 

1) Hosted plan with quota bump vs. Dedicated reserved capacity
  - Hosted + custom quotas: likely sufficient for pilot if we provision a higher per-key concurrent-request cap and token-rate allowance. Quicker to get started; supports streaming and transparent fallbacks.
  - Dedicated reserved capacity: recommended if ACME wants predictable p95 under sustained high load and strict isolation during peak events (this also reduces unit cost for heavy token usage).

2) Recommended initial quota settings (pilot):
  - Concurrent parallel requests (per-api-key): 1,500 soft concurrent limit, 2,200 hard cap (with graceful 429 + Retry-After behavior).
  - Token-per-minute allowance: 5M tokens/minute per-tenant (burstable via configured burst buckets for promo windows).
  - Connections for streaming: support for 500 long-lived streaming connections; beyond that we recommend a pooled gateway or a Dedicated deployment.

3) Backoff and retry guidance
  - We’ll provide recommended exponential backoff with jitter and a 429 handling pattern in the SDKs. For streaming connections, prefer connection pooling and multiplexing where possible.

4) Data we still need before final sizing
  - 24–72 hour anonymized traffic CSV (timestamps, request type, token in/out, response time).
  - Expected growth rate for Q2–Q4 post-pilot.

Attachments: redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf (updated with our initial numbers), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP milestones + owners).

Next steps: confirm deep-dive for Wed 10/14 10:00 PT — we’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda (infrastructure assumptions, SLA targets, and sample load test plan).

Laura/Logan — want to call out for the deep-dive: Logan please be prepared to discuss kernel-level optimizations and expected latency profile for 512/1,024 token responses; Laura please bring sample config for hosted quota changes and fallback routing.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx
